items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, Dick Hyman was one of your students, wasn't he? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes, Dick was one of my students.

ctx.x: And so far, my repertoire has four arrangements in them done from Dick Hyman, a featured piano in the Symphonic Strings. I hope to get some more; I'd like to -- there's an arranger I like very much named Glenn Osser who's very capable in this sort of thing.

items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I won a contest... the prize was twelve lessons with Teddy Wilson. So I did do that... I continued to be friends with him until he passed away a few years ago.

ctx.x: I understand you studied some with Teddy Wilson early on.

Yeah I did. I won a contest, a local radio station had a contest and the prize was twelve lessons with Teddy Wilson. So I did do that, and it was wonderful. I continued to be friends with him until he passed away a few years ago.

What was it like playing with some of the jazz legends? I mean is there one or two people that stood out in your mind from all the people you’ve played with over the years. I know you’ve played with Dizzy, and —
